title: On the Way to a Compassionate University: Experiences of Students and University Staff Dealing with Serious Illness, Dying, Death and Grief at the Universities of Cologne and Münster
summary: Topics such as serious illness, dying, death, and grief are relevant at universities as well, but are often rarely discussed there. At the same time, research shows that universities can become places that better support people in such situations. The "CaringUniversity" study looks at what students and staff at the universities of Cologne and Münster think about these problems and the kind of support they would like to receive. To do this, we are running an online survey and also conducting some interviews. The people who can take part are adult students and university staff who have had relevant experiences in their daily university life. The goal is to better understand what those affected need and to come up with ideas for a more sensitive and supportive approach at universities.
conditions: Participants aged 18 or older who are capable of giving informed consent; those reporting a serious medical condition of their own will be included regardless of the specific diagnosis

interventions.name: In this exploratory monocentre non-interventional pilot study in mixed-methods design, a one-time anonymous online survey will first be conducted among students and staff members of the Universities of Cologne and Münster (planned sample size: at least 300–500 participants). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Students and staff at the universities of Cologne and Münster who have had personal experiences with illness, dying, death, or grief in a university setting, with relevant impacts on their daily academic or professional lives.
•    Participation requires that participants have had personal experiences with serious illness, dying, death, or grief in a university setting. To account for potential recall effects, the questionnaire records the time elapsed since the event, and this is taken into account in the analysis. The target group is divided into two experience groups: Direct experiences: one’s own serious illness or health condition causing significant distress. Indirect experiences: illness, dying, or death of a close relative or friend, regardless of whether the participant played a caregiving or support role
o    Capacity to provide consent
Exclusion criteria:
•    No professional or academic affiliation with the University of Cologne or Münster
•    No personal experience with illness, dying, death, or grief, 
•    Lack of capacity to give consent
